functions.name: readSkeletonData_animationsLoop
functions.address_range: 0x28d318 outer head .. 0x28e79c back edge (B3/B4 + families + publish)
functions.semantics: Runs the B3 preamble once (readSkeletonData_animationFrameInit), then per animation: readSkeletonData_animationKeys (8 Json_getItem lookups + the legacy draworder retry), readSkeletonData_animationTimelines (B4 sum + spAnimation_create + slotsChild spill), the nine family drivers in control-flow order slots -> bones -> ik -> transform -> paths(+B17) -> deform -> drawOrder -> events, then readSkeletonData_publishAnimation and frame->animation = frame->animation->next. Returns data_raw on success; NULL as soon as a family error has disposed the animation and the skeleton data. B18 (Json_dispose of the root) is top-level and is not run here.
family_order_evidence: 0x28d4e8 beq 0x28d640 (B4 -> B6 when the slots child is NULL)
quirks: B17 is interleaved inside the paths stage: 0x28e538 bne 0x28e8ec enters it, 0x28e8fc beq 0x28e048 is the silent 'mix' skip, and 0x28ea0c b 0x28e048 returns to B13's shared node advance
the slots stage is gated on the CURRENT animation's slots node + child (0x28d4c8/0x28d4d8/0x28d4e8), never on a frame->slotsChild left by the previous animation (0x28d4e4 is its only writer)
slots rc==0 has two meanings: E1 already reported (parser+0x08 non-NULL) or the silent index==-1 branch (0x28d538 beq 0x28ea10); parser->error distinguishes them so the unowned block can run

path re-entry: the B13 driver cannot resume mid-constraint, so a synthetic map/constraint wrapper restarts it at the node's next sibling; the index cell is recomputed with the same scan because a successful findPathConstraint always makes the scan hit
deform/drawOrder handoffs are resolved by re-walking the same JSON list with the same lookups to get the exact failing node for E4/E6
the loop never calls Json_dispose; B18 stays with the top-level loader

functions.name: readSkeletonData_animationsSlotNotFound
functions.semantics: B5 slot-index -1 terminal: spAnimation_dispose(animation); setError(parser, current animation node, "Slot not found: " @0x357e7c, current slot node member key); spSkeletonData_dispose(data); return NULL.
functions.why_here: the census assigns 0x28ea10 to no functional block and c/spine_read_tl_slots stops at 0x28d538 because the bytes sit outside its window; leaving it unimplemented would drop the slot-miss error path
instruction_anchors: 0x28ea20 ldr r2,[sp,#0x2c] (current slot node; B5 rewrites it at 0x28d638)

open: README/assembly note: this module owns no new timeline bytes; the only new recovered block is 0x28ea10

the path re-entry calls spSkeletonData_findPathConstraint again per segment; that is an adapter-level extra synthetic-boundary call, not an original call count. It is exact for timeline values because the scan hits whenever the lookup succeeds

a path scan MISS after a successful lookup is unreachable with the recovered findPathConstraint shape (returns an element of the scanned array or NULL); the cross-constraint stale index therefore cannot be observed by this assembly
frame->slotsChild remains the only per-animation stack word that B4 writes conditionally; the loop's explicit gate is what keeps a previous animation's node out of the next pass
B18 (Json_dispose of the root) is deliberately not part of this module; the top-level loader must call readSkeletonData_finishAnimations after a non-NULL return
